name.text: Optimization with Lagrange Multipliers: Finding Maximum and Minimum Values

questiontext.text:
Find the maximum and the minimum values of \(f(x,y)={@a@}x^2+{@c@}y^2+{@e@}\) subject to the constraint \(g(x,y)={@b@}x^2+{@c@}y^2={@d@}\) using the Method of Lagrange Multipliers.

The absolute maximum is [[input:ans1]][[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

The absolute minimum is [[input:ans2]][[validation:ans2]][[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

Here the constraint is a sum of two terms that are squared, hence the largest possible range of \(x\) is \(\displaystyle -{@lar_xr@}\le {@lar_xr@}\) (the largest values occur if \(y=0.\)

Likewise,the largest possible range of \(y\) is \(-{@lar_yr@}\le {@lar_yr@}\) (with the largest values occurring if \(x=0\)).

Therefore, the constraint region is bounded. It is also closed, therefore it is compact. Now, by the Extreme Value Theorem, we can conclude that the function has absolute extrema in the constraint region

The next step is to write down the system of Lagrange Multiplier equations:

\(\displaystyle {@f_x@}\) \((f_x=\lambda g_x)...\) equation \(1\)

\(\displaystyle {@f_y@}\) \((f_y=\lambda g_y)...\) equation \(2\)

\(\displaystyle {@g_xy@}\) (Constraint equation) \(…\) equation \(3\)

From the second equation

\(\displaystyle {@d3@}\lambda-{@d4@}={@d4@}(\lambda-1)\)

\(\displaystyle \rightarrow y=0\) (case \(1\)) or \(\lambda=1\)(case \(2\))

Case \(1:\) when \(y=0\)

\(\displaystyle {@b@}x^2={@d@} \rightarrow x=\pm {@ta8@}\)

Hence two potential absolute extrema points are

\((\displaystyle -{@lar_xr@},0)\) and \(({@lar_xr@},0)\)

Case \(2:\) when \(\lambda =1\)

\(\displaystyle {@d1@}={@d2@} \rightarrow x={@ta11@}\)

Plugging in \(x=0\) into the constraint equation

\(\displaystyle {@c@}y^2={@d@} \rightarrow y=\pm {@ta12@}\)

This part gives us two more points that are potential absolute extrema,

\(\displaystyle (0,-{@ta12@})\) and \((0,{@ta12@})\)

To find the absolute extrema we evaluate the function at each of these points

\(\displaystyle f(-{@lar_xr@},0)={@val_x1y@}\) \(f({@lar_xr@},0)={@val_x2y@}\) \(\displaystyle f(0,-{@ta12@})={@val_y1x@}\) \(f(0,{@ta12@})={@val_y2x@}\)

The absolute maximum is then \(\displaystyle {@ta15@}\)

The absolute minimum is \(\displaystyle {@ta16@}\)
